value.rationale: The question is a natural sharp structural threshold: a universal run-based insertion list-two code is literally unique optimal for the smallest alphabets but fails at exactly four. The four-letter exchange can be packed into disjoint blocks to produce a genuinely infinite q-ary family with size gain floor(q/4), avoiding an isolated minor finite improvement. Establishes a useful short-block benchmark and explains a structural limitation of adjacent-repeat constructions without claiming a broader unknown optimum.
